findings.behavior: Every persisted retrieval episode already carries retrieval_id, turn_id, episode_id, causal_id, session_id and generation together with query_hash and selected memories.
findings.side_effects: Persists the identity/provenance tuple needed for exact later feedback binding.
findings.configuration: None specific to identity persistence in the inspected span.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream consumers can still lose causal precision if they select by session/time instead of the already-persisted exact identities.
findings.frankenstein_2_implication: Do not invent a new retrieval identity schema for this repair. Carry the existing retrieval_id/turn_id/episode_id/causal_id/generation tuple through Typed Entry, WorldSlice/GWT cognition work, and feedback reduction.

findings.behavior: The relevance judge reconstructs its query by scanning the transcript and returning the last user message, not by loading a query bound to the selected retrieval episode.
findings.side_effects: Provides text for model judging without an explicit retrieval/turn identity join.
findings.failure_mode: If Stop processing is reordered, duplicated, delayed, or multiple retrievals exist in one session, the last transcript user text can describe a different turn than the selected retrieval episode.
findings.frankenstein_2_implication: The cognition work item must carry the exact query/turn identity at admission time; transcript-last-message recovery is at most a compatibility fallback, never canonical causal binding.

findings.behavior: The Stop relevance path selects one unjudged retrieval using session_id plus ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1, then obtains the query from the transcript and applies model-derived credit to that selected row.
findings.side_effects: May write modell:relevanz feedback and update retrieval-entrypoint policy through MicroClay._apply_credit.
findings.failure_mode: Session/time selection is weaker than the exact identities already present; interleaved same-session episodes can therefore be judged against the wrong turn/query before credit is durably attached.
findings.frankenstein_2_implication: Replace newest-session selection with an exact cognition work item keyed by retrieval_id + turn_id + episode_id + causal_id + generation; reject mismatches fail-closed.

findings.behavior: Once a row has been selected, the credit receipt hash includes retrieval_id, causal_id, generation, signal_class and value, and duplicate receipt IDs are rejected.
findings.side_effects: Provides deterministic duplicate suppression for the chosen row.
findings.configuration: Learning-rate and reward-policy constants outside this span.
findings.failure_mode: Strong receipt identity after selection does not repair a wrong-row selection made earlier; deterministic credit can be causally misattached with perfect deduplication.
findings.frankenstein_2_implication: Move exact identity checking before cognition and before reduction; preserve the existing deterministic receipt idea downstream.

contradictions.claim_a: The donor already persists turn/retrieval/episode/causal/generation identity for each retrieval episode.
contradictions.claim_b: The Stop model-judge path selects by session plus newest timestamp and reconstructs the query from the latest transcript message.
contradictions.resolution: Preserve both as source facts. Frankenstein 2.0 should reuse the existing identity tuple and retire session-newest selection as canonical binding; runtime interleaving evidence is still required before claiming observed donor misattachment.

contradictions.claim_a: _apply_credit produces a deterministic receipt bound to retrieval_id/causal_id/generation after a row is chosen.
contradictions.claim_b: That deterministic receipt cannot prove the chosen row matched the user query judged by the model.
contradictions.resolution: Separate selection correctness from receipt idempotency. Both gates are required.
